newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU lets Portugal delay telecoms liberalisation.
newsitem.headline: EU lets Portugal delay telecoms liberalisation.

text.p: The European Commission said on Wednesday that Portugal could delay the complete liberalisation of its telecommunications until the beginning of 2000, two years after most other countries in the bloc must act.
It said in an initial statement that Portugal must liberalise international connections to GSM service providers by January 1, 1999.
"Regarding alternative infrastructures, the opportunity to enter the Portuguese market will be given to competitors starting in the middle of this year," it said.
Unless otherwise exempted, European Union countries are supposed to liberalise their telecoms sectors completley by January 1, 1998.

The Commission said it had granted Portugal a delay on grounds that Portugal Telecom had been forced to make substantial capital investments to improve the country's telecoms networks and needed more time to prepare properly for liberalisation. BRUSSELS NEWSROOM: +32 2 287-6830
